title: Cursor Uses S3 WAL to Scale Git Storage to More than 300 Pushes per Second
gist: Cursor built Continuity, a Git storage architecture that makes an S3-backed write-ahead log the source of truth and treats local NVMe repos as warm caches, reporting linear read scaling to 100 replicas and over 300 pushes per second on S3 Express One Zone to serve heavy CI and agent-created repositories.

insights.claim: Cursor's Continuity makes an S3-backed write-ahead log the durable source of truth for Git storage instead of relying on replica coordination for consistency.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shows a broader architectural shift toward object storage as the consistency layer, increasing reliance on cloud object storage.

insights.claim: GitHub's Spokes architecture keeps multiple NVMe replicas and uses three-phase commit for reference updates, an approach whose coordination overhead grows as replica counts increase.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Identifies scaling limits of incumbent Git hosting designs under agent-driven load.
insights.quote: coordination overhead increases as replica counts grow

insights.claim: In Continuity, a push is acknowledged only after required data is persisted to S3 and the reference update recorded in the WAL, with batching used to offset S3 PUT latency.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Durability-before-acknowledgment on object storage is a viable design for high-write developer infrastructure.

insights.claim: Cursor engineer Vicent Martí describes local NVMe repositories as warm caches rather than authoritative copies, with rendezvous hashing for preferred nodes and atomic compare-and-swap on S3 letting any server accept a push.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Stateless-compute-plus-object-storage designs reduce the operational cost of scaling replicas.

insights.claim: UDP gossip propagates WAL updates and conditional S3 reads verify replica state in under 10 milliseconds on average, and lost gossip does not affect correctness because S3 remains the source of truth.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Low-latency conditional reads make S3 practical as a coordination primitive.

insights.claim: Cursor reports linear read scaling with up to 100 replicas in synthetic tests and more than 300 pushes per second using S3 Express One Zone.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Demonstrates a demand driver for premium low-latency object storage tiers like S3 Express One Zone.

insights.claim: In synthetic tests on Cursor's everysphere monorepo, Continuity reached up to 120 pushes per second with S3 Standard versus more than 300 with S3 Express One Zone, at which point Git compaction became the bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A ~2.5x throughput gap shows storage tier choice materially drives developer-infrastructure performance.
insights.locator: In synthetic tests using Cursor's everysphere

insights.claim: Only the primary performs Git compaction while replicas download resulting packs from S3, trading bandwidth for CPU.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shifts cost from compute to data transfer, changing the cloud cost mix for such systems.

insights.claim: Casey Lee, CTO at Liatrio and a former AWS engineer, noted that Cursor's published performance figures had not been independently verified.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Benchmarks are vendor-reported and synthetic; treat headline throughput claims cautiously.

insights.claim: Continuity targets both large repositories with heavy CI workloads and the large number of smaller repositories created by coding agents, with monorepos supporting hundreds of CI replicas and idle repositories materialized on demand.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Coding agents are multiplying repositories and CI load, pressuring incumbent Git hosting and creating room for new infrastructure.

insights.claim: Maksim Al Dandan described the approach as treating Git storage like a database, raising push consistency, force-push transactions and point-in-time recovery as relevant questions.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Git hosting may increasingly adopt database-grade guarantees and tooling.
insights.locator: The storage model has prompted comparisons

insights.claim: Continuity moves the consistency boundary from the replica layer to durable object storage, trading replica coordination for storage validation, asynchronous propagation and extra bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Reflects a generalisable trend of building stateful systems on object storage.
